t: LeetCode 1960 - Maximum Product of the Length of Two Palindromic Substrings
o:
**Understanding the problem**

Choose two non-overlapping substrings, both odd-length palindromes, maximizing the product of their lengths; formally pick i <= j < k <= l with s[i..j] and s[k..l] palindromic.

Examples:
- ababbb: aba (indices 0-2) and bbb (3-5) give 3 * 3 = 9.
- zaaaxbbby: aaa and bbb give 3 * 3 = 9.

Introduce a split point: the first palindrome lives entirely in a prefix and the second entirely in the complementary suffix. With |s| up to 10^5, comparing palindromes pairwise is quadratic at best; Manacher's algorithm lists every maximal odd palindrome in O(n), after which two linear sweeps finish the job.
k: For every center, the widest odd palindrome comes from Manacher's algorithm in overall O(n).

The longest palindrome ending exactly at i satisfies end[i] >= end[i + 1] - 2: trim both ends of the one ending at i + 1. Painting full-palindrome endpoints plus this recurrence yields all exact-end values in one backward sweep.
The answer is max over split i of prefixBest(i) * suffixBest(i + 1); single characters guarantee both sides are nonempty.

a.n: Approach 1: Expand Around Centers, Then Aggregate
a.i: Expand around each center to its widest odd radius r, painting 2r + 1 into end[c + r] (where that palindrome ends) and start[c - r] (where it begins). Backward propagation end[i] = max(end[i], end[i + 1] - 2) and its forward mirror then recover, for every position, the longest palindrome ending or starting exactly there. Prefix maxima over end and suffix maxima over start give best-inside-prefix and best-inside-suffix, so every split point contributes a candidate product.
s: For each center expand to radius r; paint 2r + 1 at end[c + r] and start[c - r] when r > 0.
Propagate end right-to-left with the minus-2 rule; propagate start left-to-right.
Build prefix maxima pre over end and suffix maxima suf over start.
Return the maximum of pre[i] * suf[i + 1] over all splits.
a.t: O(n^2) - expansion degenerates on runs like aaaa; the aggregation sweeps are linear

a.i: Manacher on t = #a#b#c#... computes, in O(n), the palindromic radius p at every transformed position; at the transformed index of original center c this value is odd and equals 2 * rad + 1, where rad is the odd palindrome arm around c. Substituting rad = p[2c + 1] / 2 for the expansion step leaves painting, propagation and aggregation untouched, giving a fully linear solution.
s: Run Manacher on the #-joined string to obtain radii p.
For original center c take rad = p[2c + 1] / 2 (integer division); paint end[c + rad] and start[c - rad] with 2 * rad + 1 when rad > 0.
Apply both minus-2 propagations and build prefix/suffix maxima.
a.t: O(n) - Manacher plus four linear passes
a.sp: O(n) - the transformed string and auxiliary arrays

w: Offer Approach 1 first if Manacher is not second nature - it is correct and only degrades on pathological inputs - then upgrade to Approach 2. Pitfalls: even-length palindromes must be excluded (odd lengths only), the two substrings may not share an index (the split-point framing enforces this), and products up to (10^5)^2 overflow 32-bit types. Follow-up: allow even-length palindromes too (Manacher already reports them), or maximize the sum of lengths instead.
